text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- French authorities favour offer from Belgian group LBO with support by French media group Havas for privatisation of state-owned film producer Societe Francaise de Production (SFP).
- Chairman of tour operator Nouvelles Frontieres and Corsair airline Jacques Maillot interested in buying both AOM and Air Liberte airlines, to fend off moves on Air Liberte by British Airways.
-- Insurer UAP posts 860 million franc profit for the first half, expects 1.7 billion franc profit for 1996.
-- Credit Mutuel chairman Etienne Pflimlin says bank shows vigorous growth.
-- Two Generale des Eaux executives admit in court their group funded elected officials on the French island of La Reunion between 1990 and 1993 to secure water supply contracts.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES

-- Eurotunnel shares tumble 18 percent since requoting as debt-restructuring plans will increase number of shares and operations are not yet able to cover financial costs, expected to reach 3.2 billion francs a year.
-- Some members of the conservative majority call for a cut in value added tax from 1997 and lower taxes on fuel.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe to sign agreement today in Reims with first company implementing a plan to avoid layoffs by reducing work hours and in turn paying lower labour charges.
-- Auto parts maker Ecia, a PSA Peugeot Citroen subsidiary, allies with parts supplier Treves to become biggest shareholder of Bertrand Faure.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Cabinet meeting adopts bill limiting health spending to a 1.7 percent rise in 1997, plans to curb 1997 social security deficit to 29.7 billion francs from 49.2 in 1996. Parliament needs to approve plan.
-- Bouygues floats 40 percent of oil drilling subsidiary Bouygues Offshore in offer expected to generate between 755 million and one billion francs.
-- Saint-Gobain discloses holds more than 10 percent of Suez voting rights after payment of dividends in Suez shares and doubling of voting rights on shares held longer than two years.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Eurotunnel's small shareholders bitter about tumble in the value of their holdings.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE

-- The European Commission sought to silence a German scientist who warned about a risk to human health from mad cow disease more than one year before Britain admitted a probable hazard, an investigating committee of the European Parliament disclosed on Wednesday.
